note: Patcher matrix for B185, built from main at 01973e0 (#265). AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID 7449502 AND WAS WRONG: the build ran after #265 merged, not before. That mattered -- a reviewer read the stale commit, correctly observed that two label fixes landed after 7449502, and concluded the artifact predated them. It does not. f290649 is an ancestor of 01973e0, and 01973e0's generator is byte-identical to main's, so the four label fixes are all in what was built. Checkable rather than asserted -- against work/patch_mobile_furniture_pack.py at 01973e0: VF2ScanLabelGroup 8, VF2BehaviorLabelStillFromThisSession 6, VF2BehaviorLabelSlotIsCurrentFor 3, the praise-restart writeback 1, VF2GetVillagerCachedBehaviorLabel 5. THOSE COUNTS ARE STATEMENTS ABOUT THE GENERATOR, NOT ABOUT THE ARTIFACT, and so are the ancestry and blob-equality checks -- none of them inspects a B185 executable. The artifact-level evidence is separate: all 32 B185 executables differ from the B184 build they were seeded from. THAT SHOWS THE EXECUTABLES WERE REBUILT AND NOTHING NARROWER -- a full relink changes every hash whether or not any given feature is in it. What it does rule out is a seeded build inheriting the previous release's executable untouched, which has been a real failure mode here, and the check was validated in both directions before being relied on: a genuine cross-release pair (B181 against B184) differs 32 of 32, and a release compared against itself differs 0 of 32, so it discriminates rebuilt from not-rebuilt. IT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE FIX-PRESENT FROM FIX-ABSENT, and no search of the executable can either, because symbol names do not survive linking. The honest chain is: the generator that ran is byte-identical to main's and contains the four fixes, the binaries were rebuilt from it, and the last link -- from that code to what a player sees -- is closed only by playing the game. Everything merged since the build is test files and this directory's identities data, so no rebuild is required. Seeded per variant from the B184 matrix outputs, NOT from B181: VF2 builds INHERIT assets from the seed, so a seed older than the previous release silently drops the art that release added and the build still reports success. All 32 seed directories were confirmed to exist before this file was written, because a seed directory is created before anything links, so an interrupted run leaves a directory that satisfies no payload contract. B185 EXISTS FOR FIVE MERGED CHANGES THAT B184 PREDATES: #256 (says where the overlay-guard residual is actually defended) and FOUR LABEL FIXES that only together finish the job -- #261 (labels re-roll once a behaviour actually ends), #262 (the session gate anchors on the villager it was handed, not on a global naming the last villager to enter a wrapped native behaviour), #264 (accepting a praise restart advances the cached record, without which the SECOND praise of the same action re-rolled the caption) and #265 (the applier's own cache read was still global-guarded, so a group's keep-the-native-label choice could flip to a mod caption mid-action). Each of the last three was found only after the previous one looked complete, and each would have produced the OPPOSITE regression -- a caption changing during an action rather than never changing between them). The label fix is the player-visible one -- before it, the Home Gym showed one action out of ten and all 47 label groups were equally frozen, because the PERSISTENT label text at villager+0x1BBA8 survives the end of a behaviour and was being read as 'this villager is already doing X'. Export with work/export_release_bundle.py, NEVER work/export_offline_patch_bundle.py directly: B183 shipped twelve features short precisely because the low-level exporter was called directly and the wrapper's guards -- one of which refuses a build whose overlays would be silently absent -- never ran. The B184 seeds must NOT be moved, renamed or deleted: they are inputs to this build, not stale outputs. NOTE ON THE SEED EXECUTABLES: seeds supply ASSETS only; every overlay must be rebuilt from current main and verified individually (faulty 84c0590f85 absent, fixed 84c05974065b present), because nothing anywhere in the release path inspects overlay bytes and that check is the only thing preventing a guard-passing release from shipping the startup crash.
